hints.content:
Pierre started with $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Let’s follow the construction step-by-step to understand which of the statements is useful for justifying that $\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$ are right angles.

Pierre constructed points $C$ and $D$ so that $\overline{BC} \cong \overline{BD}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Line A B. A circle arc is centered at point B and intersects line A B at point D on one side and point C on the other side.

hints.content:
Then he constructed point $E$ so that $\overline{CE} \cong \overline{DE}$.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Line A B. A circle arc is centered at point B and intersects line A B at point D on one side and point C on the other side. Another circle arc has the center at point D. It passes through a point E not on line A B. A third circle arc has its center at C and intersects at point E as well.

Line A B. A circle arc is centered at point B and intersects line A B at point D on one side and point C on the other side. Another circle arc has the center at point D. It passes through a point E not on line A B. A third circle arc has its center at C and intersects at point E as well. A line passes through points B and E.

hints.content:
As a result, we have $\triangle CBE \cong \triangle DBE$ by side-side-side congruence.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Line A B. A circle arc is centered at point B and intersects line A B at point D on one side and point C on the other side. Another circle arc has the center at point D. It passes through a point E not on line A B. A third circle arc has its center at C and intersects at point E as well. A line passes through points B and E. Dashed segments B D, B E, and D E make triangle D B E. Dashed segments B C, B E, and C E make triangle C B E. Sides CE and D E are congruent. Sides B C and B D are congruent. Sides B E and E B are congruent.

hints.content:
And $\angle 1 \cong \angle 2$ since they are corresponding parts of congruent triangles. They also form a linear pair, so their measures must add to $180 \degree$. This means they must also both be right angles.


[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Line A B. A circle arc is centered at point B and intersects line A B at point D on one side and point C on the other side. Another circle arc has the center at point D. It passes through a point E not on line A B. A third circle arc has its center at C and intersects at point E as well. A line passes through points B and E. Dashed segments B D, B E, and D E make triangle D B E. Dashed segments B C, B E, and C E make triangle C B E. Sides CE and D E are congruent. Sides B C and B D are congruent. Sides B E and E B are congruent. Angle C B E is labeled one. Angle D B E is labeled two.

hints.content: So, $\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$ are right angles because they are corresponding angles in congruent triangles that form a linear pair.

question.content:
Pierre constructed line $\overleftrightarrow{BE}$ perpendicular to line $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

**Which of the following statements best justifies why $\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$ are right angles?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: Line A B. A circle arc is centered at point B and intersects line A B at point D on one side and point C on the other side. Another circle arc has the center at point D. It passes through a point E not on line A B.  A third circle arc has its center at C and intersects at point E as well. A line passes through points B and E. It is a perpendicular bisector to line A B at point B.

choices.content: They are corresponding angles in congruent triangles that form a linear pair.
They are vertical angles, and all vertical angles are right angles.
When lines are parallel, same-side interior angles are right angles.
Lines perpendicular to the same transversal create right angles.
